channel.title: AI Threat Watch: Model & data leak
channel.description: Verified case files in the category Model & data leak.

item.title: [HIGH] AP/Seattle Times obtain ~3,500 unredacted student files flagged by Gaggle AI monitoring in Vancouver, WA
item.description: A records request by The Seattle Times and AP returned links to nearly 3,500 unredacted screenshots of student writing flagged by Gaggle's AI surveillance, covering suicide, depression, abuse and sexuality, viewable by anyone with the link and without a password. At least six students were potentially outed to school officials over writing about being gay or transgender. Target: Students of Vancouver Public Schools, Washington. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Whistleblower says LAUSD's $6M 'Ed' AI chatbot sent student data offshore before vendor AllHere collapsed
item.description: A former AllHere engineering director alleged the 'Ed' chatbot built for Los Angeles Unified put students' personal data in every AI prompt, shared it with third parties and processed most requests on overseas servers. LAUSD shut the chatbot down after AllHere furloughed most staff in June 2024 and said student data remained protected. Target: Students of Los Angeles Unified School District. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Aoki infostealer expands to steal Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor credentials
item.description: The Aoki (Aokigahara) infostealer, first seen earlier in 2026, now collects credentials and session files from AI coding assistants, putting developer identities and connected infrastructure at risk. Target: Developers' Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor credentials and sessions. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] BodySwap sexual deepfake platform breach exposes about 10,300 user accounts
item.description: User account data from BodySwap, a sexual deepfake platform, was reported leaked: about 10,300 accounts per French Breaches, about 10,000 customers per Libération. Target: BodySwap deepfake platform and its users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Microsoft AI researchers expose 38TB of data via misconfigured SAS token
item.description: Wiz Research found Microsoft's AI GitHub repository exposed 38TB of data, including over 30,000 internal Teams messages, because of one misconfigured SAS token. Target: Microsoft AI GitHub repository. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] PixelLeak: AI coding agents push 13,000 internal screenshots to public GitHub
item.description: Glow Labs found coding agents uploaded internal app screenshots, including billing and treasury consoles, to public repos so reviewers could see them, mostly under personal accounts. Target: 300+ organizations' developers. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-16008: Xiaomi replayed MiMo user sessions through Claude via 1,500 accounts
item.description: Anthropic says Xiaomi replayed real MiMo user sessions through Claude via OpenClaw and OpenCode to collect training data, 400,000+ requests across 1,500+ accounts, exposing users' names and corporate data. Target: Anthropic Claude and MiMo end users' data. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] GTG-16006: Zhipu accused of cyber-focused distillation of Claude Opus through 273 accounts
item.description: Anthropic says Zhipu (Z.ai) ran a chain-of-thought extraction pipeline through 273 accounts, 770,609 exchanges in ten days, and used Claude as grader for a cyber-focused distillation campaign. Target: Claude Opus 4.8 and another US lab's frontier model. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [CRITICAL] GTG-16005: Anthropic says Alibaba ran 151M-exchange distillation of Claude to train Qwen
item.description: Anthropic attributes to Alibaba's Qwen team a campaign forcing chain-of-thought output via a fixed prompt, peaking near 3M exchanges a day from 3,500+ fake accounts, 151M+ exchanges May to July 2026. Target: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.7 reasoning outputs. US. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Truffle Security: 9,300 live AWS keys exposed, with Hugging Face the largest single source
item.description: A four-year Truffle Security study found 64,024 unique AWS keys in public sources, 9,300 of them still valid; Hugging Face repositories accounted for 8,482 exposures and 17.9 percent of those were root keys. Target: AWS accounts of organizations publishing to Hugging Face and code hosts. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Unauthorized group accesses Anthropic's restricted Claude Mythos model via vendor
item.description: Bloomberg reported a small group reached the restricted cyber-capable Mythos model using a contractor's account and a guessed URL; Anthropic investigated a third-party vendor environment. Target: Anthropic Claude Mythos Preview. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Researcher: free Lovable account could read source, Supabase keys and chats of pre-Nov 2025 projects
item.description: A researcher posting as weezerOSINT disclosed that any free Lovable account could access other users' source code, Supabase database credentials, AI chat histories and connected customer data for projects created before November 2025. Target: Lovable projects created before November 2025. SE. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Claude Code source map leak followed by malware-laced fake 'leak' repos
item.description: Anthropic accidentally shipped a source map exposing ~513,000 lines of Claude Code; attackers then used fake leaked-code GitHub repos to spread malware to developers. Target: Anthropic Claude Code / developers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Meta AI agent's flawed advice exposes sensitive data to employees for two hours
item.description: An engineer acted on an internal AI agent's faulty guidance, making large amounts of sensitive user and company data visible to unauthorized staff for about two hours. Target: Meta internal systems. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Autonomous AI agent breaches McKinsey's Lilli chatbot platform in two hours
item.description: CodeWall's offensive agent found SQL injection via unauthenticated Lilli API endpoints, claiming read-write access to 46.5M chat messages and system prompts; McKinsey patched within a day. Target: McKinsey Lilli AI platform. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Anthropic accuses DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax of distilling Claude via 24,000 accounts
item.description: Anthropic said three Chinese labs used fraudulent account networks and proxies to run 16M+ Claude exchanges to extract capabilities for their own models. Target: Anthropic Claude. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Infostealer captures OpenClaw gateway token, device keys and agent memory files
item.description: Hudson Rock documented the first infostealer log containing an OpenClaw .openclaw directory: openclaw.json with a gateway auth token, device.json with signing keys and soul.md and memory files holding private messages and calendar data. Target: OpenClaw users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Moltbook AI-agent social network exposes 1.5M agent API tokens
item.description: Wiz found Moltbook's Supabase database lacked row-level security, letting anyone read and write 1.5M agent tokens, 35,000 emails and private messages containing third-party API keys. Target: Moltbook. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Chat & Ask AI app leaks ~300M messages from 25M users via open Firebase
item.description: A researcher found the popular AI chat wrapper's Firebase rules left full chat histories readable, exposing about 300 million messages tied to more than 25 million users. Target: Codeway Chat & Ask AI. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [HIGH] Tens of thousands of OpenClaw agent gateways exposed online leaking API keys and chats
item.description: After the viral OpenClaw agent framework spread, researchers found its gateway bound to public interfaces without authentication on tens of thousands of hosts, exposing API keys, credentials and private chat histories. Target: Self-hosted OpenClaw (Clawdbot/Moltbot) instances. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Microsoft 365 Copilot bug summarises confidential emails despite DLP policies
item.description: Microsoft confirmed (CW1226324) that a code error let Copilot Chat's work tab read and summarise Drafts and Sent Items emails carrying labels such as Confidential despite DLP policies. A fix rolled out in February 2026. Target: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat customers. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] OpenAI API user data exposed in breach of analytics vendor Mixpanel
item.description: An attacker who smished Mixpanel exported a dataset with names, emails and coarse locations of OpenAI API users; OpenAI said no chats, keys or payment data were exposed. Target: OpenAI API platform users. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Vyro AI leaves 116GB of ImagineArt and Chatly prompts and tokens on open Elasticsearch
item.description: Cybernews found an unauthenticated Elasticsearch server belonging to Vyro AI streaming about 116GB of live logs with user prompts, bearer tokens and user agents from apps with over 10 million downloads. Target: Vyro AI (ImagineArt, Chatly, Chatbotx apps). PK. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Cisco Talos finds over 1,100 Ollama LLM servers open to the internet without authentication
item.description: A Shodan sweep by Cisco Talos located more than 1,100 publicly reachable Ollama servers within minutes; about 20 percent were actively serving models open to extraction, jailbreak and resource abuse. Target: Self-hosted Ollama deployments. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Over 370,000 Grok conversations exposed in Google search via share links
item.description: Forbes found Grok's share button generated indexable URLs, so search engines surfaced hundreds of thousands of user chats, some with personal, medical or credential details. Target: xAI Grok users. GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Microsoft 365 Copilot summarised files without writing audit log entries
item.description: Pistachio CTO Zack Korman found that asking Copilot to omit the reference link when summarising a file produced no audit record, letting insiders read documents without a trace. Microsoft fixed it on 17 August 2025. Target: Microsoft 365 Copilot enterprise customers. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Thousands of shared ChatGPT conversations surface in Google search; OpenAI kills feature
item.description: A Make this chat discoverable toggle on shared links let search engines index conversations; Fast Company found thousands via site:chatgpt.com/share, some with personal details. OpenAI removed the feature. Target: OpenAI ChatGPT users. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Wiz finds auth bypass exposing private enterprise apps on Wix's Base44 platform
item.description: Wiz Research found undocumented register and verify-otp endpoints that needed only a public app_id to create verified accounts on private Base44 apps, bypassing SSO. Wix fixed it within 24 hours of the 9 July report. Target: Base44 (Wix) AI app platform. IL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Exposed llama.cpp servers leak user prompts through the /slots debug endpoint
item.description: UpGuard found about 400 internet-facing llama.cpp servers, a third of which exposed live prompts via the unauthenticated /slots endpoint; 952 messages were collected in a day, including sexual roleplay involving fictional minors. Target: Self-hosted llama.cpp inference servers. GL. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Meta AI bug let any logged-in user read other people's private prompts and replies
item.description: AppSecure's Sandeep Hodkasia found that changing the guessable ID of an edited prompt returned another user's prompt and reply because Meta skipped authorisation checks. Meta fixed it in January 2025 and paid $10,000. Target: Meta AI chatbot. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] DOGE staffer Marko Elez leaks xAI API key granting access to 52 Grok models
item.description: Marko Elez, a DOGE employee with access to sensitive federal databases, committed a script containing a private xAI API key to public GitHub; researchers found it unlocked at least 52 xAI models and it was still valid after the repo was pulled. Target: xAI private LLMs including grok-4-0709. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] McDonald's McHire AI hiring bot exposed up to 64M applicant records via '123456' login
item.description: Researchers accessed the admin panel of the Olivia hiring chatbot with default 123456 credentials and an IDOR flaw, exposing chat logs and contact data tied to up to 64M applications. Target: McDonald's / Paradox.ai. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Asana MCP server logic flaw exposed customer data across organisations for a month
item.description: A logic bug in Asana's new MCP server, live from early May, could show tasks, project metadata, comments and files from other organisations to users of AI tools. Asana took it offline on 5 June and fixed it. Target: Asana MCP server customers. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Meta AI app's Discover feed broadcasts users' private medical and legal chats
item.description: The Meta AI app's public Discover feed showed conversations users appeared to have shared by accident, including medical, financial and legal details, because the share flow gave no clear warning. Meta added a warning. Target: Meta AI app users. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Lovable-built apps leak user data: 303 endpoints across 170 projects lacked row-level security
item.description: Researcher Matt Palmer found Lovable-generated Supabase backends shipped without working row-level security, letting anyone read or write tables; a scan of 1,645 apps found 170 exposing emails, phones, payment data and API keys. Target: Apps generated by the Lovable AI app builder. SE. Verification: disputed.

item.title: [HIGH] xAI employee leaks API key on GitHub exposing 60 private Grok models for two months
item.description: An xAI technical staffer committed an x.ai API key to a public GitHub repo; GitGuardian found it granted access to at least 60 unreleased and private models, some fine-tuned on SpaceX and Tesla data, and it stayed valid for two months. Target: xAI private and fine-tuned LLMs. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Korea's PIPC: DeepSeek sent Korean users' prompts to ByteDance-linked Volcano Engine
item.description: Korea's PIPC found DeepSeek sent user data and AI prompts to five firms in China and the US, including ByteDance affiliate Volcano Engine, without consent, and ordered corrective measures. Target: South Korean DeepSeek app users. KR. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [MEDIUM] Copilot serves code from 20,000 GitHub repos that were made private, via Bing cache
item.description: Lasso Security found Copilot still returned content from over 20,000 repositories of 16,000+ organisations that had been made private or deleted, because Bing cached them while public. Microsoft disabled cache links. Target: Microsoft Copilot and GitHub repository owners. US. Verification: confirmed.

item.title: [HIGH] Hacker 'Gloomer' claims OmniGPT breach leaking 34M chat lines and 30K user contacts
item.description: A BreachForums user posted data allegedly taken from OmniGPT: about 34 million lines of user-chatbot conversations, emails and phone numbers of roughly 30,000 users and links to uploaded files containing API keys and credentials. Target: OmniGPT (multi-model AI chat aggregator). GL. Verification: reported.

item.title: [MEDIUM] OpenAI says it has evidence DeepSeek distilled its models through blocked API accounts
item.description: OpenAI told the Financial Times it found signs DeepSeek used its outputs to train a rival in breach of its terms; Microsoft reportedly saw accounts pulling large data volumes via the API and blocked them. No proof shown. Target: OpenAI models (via API). CN. Verification: disputed.

item.title: [HIGH] DeepSeek leaves ClickHouse database with chat logs and API secrets open
item.description: Wiz found a publicly reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse database exposing over a million log lines including user chat history, API secrets and backend details; it was locked down after disclosure. Target: DeepSeek. CN. Verification: reported.
